title: Epic: TUI Component Architecture (Bubble Tea + Ink-inspired ergonomics)
acceptance_criteria: internal/tui uses a small reusable component layer (StatusBar, LiveRegion, ToolSpinner, PermissionPrompt, HistoryView, InputArea) while remaining pure Go + Bubble Tea
Main Model is significantly smaller and compositional
No visual or behavioral change to the TUI (snapshot + e2e tests pass)
Future Phase 2/3 features (Command Palette, enhanced Live Status Bar with Guard, Multi-Agent views) become much cheaper to implement
All new components have isolated unit tests; existing tests updated with no regressions
Design docs (07-tui.md, 18-tui-roadmap.md, 19-tui-test-strategy.md) and AGENTS.md updated to reflect the new structure
PermissionPrompt (including batch), HistoryView, and InputArea are extracted as additional components
All knowledge beads in beads/tui-components.jsonl marked as realized; epic closed cleanly
notes:
## Context
Long design discussion (2026-05-25) on selectively adopting Ink mental model (component-based reusable UI pieces with <Box>/<Text>-style thinking) while staying 100% in Bubble Tea / Lipgloss / Glamour. Confirmed that React/Ink itself must never be introduced.

Strong alignment with existing design/07-tui.md (Elm architecture rationale) and design/18-tui-roadmap.md (Phase 2 "Live Agent Status Bar" and Command Palette are natural consumers of a component model; Phase 3 Multi-Agent Coordination View is the big payoff).

Current TUI is already well-architected but suffers from a large god Model (956 lines in model.go) and manual layout in view.go. Live region and status bar logic are already cleanly separated as view helpers — perfect extraction candidates.

## Key Artifacts from Discussion
- beads/tui-components.jsonl (knowledge capture with full proposed structs, View() implementations, migration tactics)
- Proposed dir: internal/tui/components/{statusbar,liveregion,toolspinner,permissionprompt,input,historyview}/ + core/types.go + styles/

## Migration Strategy (from conversation)
1. ToolSpinner (tiny)
2. StatusBar (always-visible, low risk)
3. LiveRegion + streaming + active tools (biggest immediate win)
4. PermissionPrompt (already half-factored in permission.go)
5. Input + HistoryView later

During transition: keep original Model fields as source of truth and sync into components (dual-state period). Delete duplicates only after full cutover + green tests.

## Non-Goals
- Do not bring any React, Ink, Yoga, or Node/Bun dependency.
- Do not over-abstract early (no heavy core.Component interface until 4+ components exist).

## Related
- design/07-tui.md (architectural foundation)
- design/18-tui-roadmap.md (Phase 2 Live Status Bar + Command Palette are direct beneficiaries)
- beads/tui-components.jsonl (detailed specs + code sketches)
- internal/tui/model.go, view.go, styles.go, permission.go (current implementation)

## Expanded Children (added 2026-05-27)
- dcode-007: PermissionPrompt extraction (easy win, already partially factored in permission.go)
- dcode-008: HistoryView extraction (viewport + renderedTurn list)
- dcode-009: InputArea extraction (textarea + autocomplete + message queue banner)
- dcode-010: Final documentation sweep, roadmap alignment, knowledge bead sync, and epic closure

Full migration order now documented in updated plan.md under thoughts/dcode-001/.


## Execution Reality (post-crap-analysis hygiene + full delivery)

**What actually shipped (beyond initial Week 1 plan):**

- Full component layer realized: StatusBar, LiveRegion (+ToolSpinner), PermissionPrompt (single+batch), HistoryView, InputArea.
- Dual-state migration executed safely (legacy fields kept as source-of-truth during extraction, then ownership moved + fields/paths deleted in consolidation passes).
- HistoryView consolidation (dcode-008): legacy m.history + m.viewport removed; HistoryView is sole owner.
- LiveRegion consolidation: m.activeTools, m.pendingDone, m.toolOrder, m.streamLines deleted; Live owns ActiveTools/CompletedTools/Drain + streaming.
- PermissionPrompt full extraction + deletion of internal/tui/permission.go (old render methods + jsonPreview moved, file removed).
- Styles centralization: internal/tui/styles/colors.go created; all Col* AdaptiveColors + lipgloss styles moved out of individual components and model/view; 5+ components updated to import.
- Dead code removal: viewInput/viewAutoComplete fully excised (0% coverage stubs deleted), old permission render paths gone.
- Guard integration (real): pkg/guardclient wired, assessPermissionRisk (file-sensitive + bash dangerous patterns), SetGuardRisk, GuardRiskLevel/Reason fields on Model, StatusBar renders "● CAUTION (reason)" + high-risk red styling.
- Command Palette foundation (Week 2+): commandpalette/ package with Command struct (ActionKey, Category, Shortcut, RiskLevel), semantic actions (not just text injection), buildCommandPaletteCommands + executePaletteAction, Ctrl+K wiring, palette overlay in View.
- Coverage push: new strip_test.go (100% on stripCursorPositionReports, stripTerminalOSCResponses, stripStandaloneBackslashLines, etc. — security-adjacent paste sanitizers); renderMarkdown coverage improved; heavy input paths exercised.
- All 20+ snapshot + model + permission_fuzz + e2e tests green with **zero drift** throughout every consolidation step.
- Model.go reduced from 1290-line god object peak; now orchestration + component delegation. View() is clean composition of 4 regions + overlays.

**Dual-state technique (the key enabler):** Legacy fields (m.history, m.activeTools, etc.) + component fields lived side-by-side. Mutations hit both during transition. Once every call site and test was updated to prefer components, the legacy paths and fields were deleted in focused passes (HistoryView first, then LiveRegion, then Permission + permission.go). InputArea kept a lighter sync bridge (syncInputArea) because its legacy textarea/queue fields are still heavily used by key handlers and history recall.

**Beads hygiene note:** Early dcode-002–007 remained "open" with planning text even after real code landed in 008/009 + follow-up consolidation work. This sweep corrects that mismatch.

**Design docs updated in this hygiene pass:** 07-tui.md, 18-tui-roadmap.md, 19-tui-test-strategy.md, 20-week-1..., AGENTS.md.

**Related artifacts:** thoughts/dcode-00[2-9]/ (execution.md + status), beads/tui-components.jsonl (knowledge beads now realized).

Epic closed cleanly. Future work (deeper Guard on tool results, custom command registration API for palette, more renderMarkdown coverage, InputArea full ownership move) tracked separately.

title: Extract LiveRegion + ToolSpinner components (core streaming + tool activity area)
acceptance_criteria:
internal/tui/components/toolspinner/toolspinner.go extracted (replaces inline activeTool + spinner creation)
internal/tui/components/liveregion/liveregion.go extracted with full logic (active tools + last N lines of stream preview + softenAssistantParagraphBreaks)
ToolStartEvent / ToolDoneEvent / TextDeltaEvent / DoneEvent paths create and mutate LiveRegion state instead of (or in addition to) Model fields
Spinner.TickMsg forwarding updated (or delegated)
viewLiveRegion() deleted; replaced by m.LiveRegion.View() call
Streaming preview and tool spinners continue to render identically (golden tests + manual verification)
Component has its own small test covering spinner rows + truncated streaming text
notes:
## Highest value extraction
This is the "live" part of the TUI that users stare at most during agent runs. Moving it into its own component with clear ownership makes future enhancements (richer tool cards, progress, Guard risk badges, etc.) tractable.

## Important details from current code
- streamBuf vs streamLines split (raw for final Glamour, stripped for live preview)
- pendingDone buffer flushed on DoneEvent
- toolOrder slice for stable rendering order (maps are random)
- lastLines() + soften... live in view.go and assistant_spacing.go

All of this moves into (or is called by) LiveRegion.

## Spinner tick ownership
Current: Model holds activeTools map and loops on TickMsg. New: LiveRegion can own the map of *toolspinner.ToolSpinner. Decide on forwarding vs component returning its own tick Cmds.

## References
- Primary spec: beads/tui-components.jsonl tui-comp-004 and tui-comp-005
- Current: model.go:39 (activeTool), 478 (ToolStartEvent), 454 (TickMsg), 107 (viewLiveRegion in view.go), assistant_spacing.go

## Week 1 Granular Breakdown
- dcode-012: ToolSpinner component + test
- dcode-013: LiveRegion core (streaming + tools) + test

## Actual Delivery
- components/toolspinner/toolspinner.go + _test.go (spinner rows for active tools).
- components/liveregion/liveregion.go + _test.go owns ActiveTools map, ToolOrder, CompletedTools, StreamLines, streaming preview, DrainCompletedTools.
- viewLiveRegion deleted; all ToolStart/Done/TextDelta/DoneEvent paths route through Live.
- Major consolidation pass (post dcode-008/009 + crap analysis): deleted m.activeTools, m.pendingDone, m.toolOrder, m.streamLines from Model; Live is now the only source of truth.
- Zero snapshot drift. Isolated tests cover spinners + streaming truncation.
